home.tutorialPitch: First time here? A short tutorial day is waiting for you.
home.tip.1: Tip: Sellers who don't know what they have sometimes bring in a real treasure.
home.tip.2: Tip: Every tool costs shop time. Don't use all of them on every item.
home.tip.3: Tip: Greedy sellers lose patience fast; desperate ones bend more easily.
home.tip.4: Tip: The General page of the catalogue lists the rules that give dates away.
play.loupeHint: Slide the loupe over the item.
play.closingSoon: It's past 5 pm. Closing time is near.
play.closed: 6 pm. The shutters come down; the remaining customers will come back tomorrow.
play.claimUnknown: The seller has no idea what it is.
tool.loupe.desc: Lets you read tiny details such as serial numbers, dates and hallmarks.
tool.scale.desc: Measures weight. Plated watches and fake coins come up light.
tool.caliper.desc: Measures a coin's diameter to the millimetre.
tool.touchstone.desc: Reveals what a metal really is: gold, or brass?
tool.uv.desc: Shows glowing paint and signatures added to a painting later.
tool.pigment.desc: Lists the pigments in a painting. Some pigments didn't exist before a certain year.

cat.title: Catalogue
cat.locked: You don't own this volume yet. You can buy it in the shop.
gen.steel: Stainless steel was invented in 1913. An older watch can't be made of it.
gen.lume: Glow-in-the-dark numerals weren't used before 1910. They shine green under the UV lamp.
gen.canvas: Synthetic canvas didn't exist before the 1950s. You can tell it by its smooth, shiny surface.
gen.uv: Under UV light, old varnish looks greenish. A signature added later glows bright white.
gen.weightsNote: Plated watches weigh less than the metal they imitate.
gen.tolerance: A deviation of ±0.3 in coin weight and diameter is normal.
gen.clueless: Sellers who don't know what they have sometimes bring in a real treasure for pennies.
shop.title: Shop
shop.cantAfford: Not enough cash in the till.
catalog.coin.desc: Coins of six rulers. Customers start bringing coins.
catalog.painting.desc: Works of six painters. Customers start bringing paintings.
tut.1: Welcome to your shop! Customers will bring you items. Your job: buy the genuine ones at a good price and refuse the fakes.
tut.2: Look at every side of the item: dial, case back and movement. Tap the tabs.
tut.3: To read tiny details, turn on the 🔍 Loupe and slide your finger over the item.
tut.4: 📖 The catalogue is your rulebook. Check the maker's years, hallmark and serial format there.
tut.5: Every tool costs shop time. At 6 pm the shutters come down.
tut.6: When you've decided, tap Buy or Refuse. You can haggle when you buy.

coll.explain: Gather one genuine work by every maker, ruler and painter in your showcase. Each piece earns visitor income worth {pct}% of its value every day you open the shop. Complete a section to earn {money}.
coll.needCatalog: You'll need the {catalog} for this section first.

coll.homeEmpty: Start by keeping a genuine piece in your showcase.
intro.1: Your grandfather's old shop is yours now. Dusty shelves, a creaky door, and a leather-bound notebook in the counter drawer.
intro.2: On the first page is his dream: to gather one genuine work by eighteen great masters in a single showcase. He never managed it.
intro.3: The market is full of fakes. Pick up the loupe, read the catalogue closely, haggle well. You'll be the one to finish the collection.
